title: Speedy Haloumi and Zucchini Salad
subtitle: with Olives and Crunchy Croutons
description: Five easy steps, minimal pans and prep… we cut the fluff but not the flavour in our speedy recipes. In just 20 minutes, you’ll have this masterpiece on the table and be crowned in glory too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 200C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Peel the zucchini into ribbons with a vegetable peeler. Crush ½ garlic clove. Cut the bread rolls into 1cm-thick slices. Slice the haloumi. Put the zucchini in a large bowl, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat.

Make croutons: Put the bread on the lined tray and drizzle with olive oil. Bake for 5-7 mins until golden and crunchy. Meanwhile, put the almonds in a cold medium frypan over medium heat. Toast, tossing, for 3-4 mins until evenly golden. Remove from the pan.

Cook haloumi and zucchini: Heat a drizzle of olive oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Cook the haloumi for 2 mins each side or until golden. Remove from the pan. Add the zucchini to the pan and cook, turning occasionally, for 2 mins or until just tender. Remove from the pan.
Make dressing: Combine the garlic, South American seasoning, 2 tsp olive oil, 1 tbs white wine vinegar and 1 tbs honey in a large bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Serve up: Add the haloumi, zucchini, croutons, spinach and olives to the dressing and gently toss to combine. Divide the salad among bowls and scatter over the toasted almonds. Enjoy!

Did you know?: Haloumi is a brined, slightly springy cheese originally from Cyprus. Traditionally it was made from a mixture of goat and sheep milk, although these days cow's milk is also used. The haloumi we use is made using vegetable rennet, so it's suitable for vegetarians.
